question: Assume today is 2026-09-08. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of births registered in Taiwan in September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics.

target.what: Number of births registered in Taiwan during September 2026, as reported in the Ministry of the Interior's monthly household registration statistics; interpreted as the count of birth-registration events recorded by registration date during 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30.
target.publisher: Ministry of the Interior, Taiwan (MOI), Department of Household Registration / MOI statistics
target.caveats: As of 2026-09-08 the target month is future/only partly elapsed, so the value must be forecast. MOI monthly household-registration births are counts by registration date, not necessarily by date of occurrence; they include delayed registrations of earlier births and exclude September births register

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 registered births can be projected from the recent level/trend in monthly birth registrations and the historical September seasonal factor; the same month in prior years and the latest months before the cutoff constrain the level.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly counts of birth registrations in Taiwan from MOI for 2021 through August 2026 if available, especially September 2021-2025 and recent 2025-2026 months; note any revisions and whether counts are by registration date.

assessment.note: Same July 2026 MOI release: p1 gives births, p4/p5 the year-on-year change, p6 the annualised crude birth rate, and the population/death/marriage figures are context. They agree internally but are not independent measurements.
May 2026 release. p2 and p16 are duplicate reports of the same 6,832 May births; p18 is the April-to-May change; p21/p22 are rate and minutes-per-birth conversions. One underlying MOI series.

2026 monthly and cumulative birth reports. p42/p43/p44 imply the record-low February and the weak January-February total; p45 is the 2025 comparator. Values are mutually consistent where periods overlap, but several are duplicate printings of the same MOI release.
Official RIS/MOI 2025 monthly and annual data. The 2025 monthly values sum to p97 (107,812), and p114 plus December helps confirm the annual total. These are the cleanest target-history points.
Secondary-source copies of the same 2025 monthly MOI/RIS birth registrations. They corroborate the official table but add no independent information; several are exact duplicates.
These are mislabelled by year. The quoted rows are 民國100/102/103 (2011/2013/2014), not 2021/2023/2024. Using them as recent annual births would be wrong.

Historical September table fragments conflict. p124's 3,189 is a decrease, not a September 2024 level; p125 says September 2025 was 27.04% below September 2024, which implies about 11,792 September 2024 births, so p64's 13,837 cannot be used as the same level. p65/p66 repeat a suspicious 13,421. Only p125 is usable as a change-rate clue.
These are 2025 forecasts, now superseded by the actual 2025 annual total p97. They are not 2026 anchors and their miss does not directly determine September 2026.

September 2026 calendar evidence. p181 is the clearest: four-day Mid-Autumn/Teachers' Day break on 25-28 September 2026. Holiday closure may delay some month-end registrations, but this is a small timing effect, not a level.

Misparsed quantities. p47's 2,200 is a month-on-month decrease, not January level; p116's 三月份 means March, not three months; p117's 100,000,000 is not a monthly birth threshold; p139's 855 is an October-versus-September change, not a September level.
Fertility-attitude and obstetric-capacity context. They describe long-run downward pressure but do not supply a monthly registration level or a September 2026 conversion factor.

methods.label: m1
methods.rationale: Own-history monthly route using the kept 2025 RIS monthly birth series and 2026 observations through July. It anchors September 2025 with p85 and lets code use the recent 2026 level and seasonal month pattern. Main limitations are missing March 2026 and August 2026 and possible registration-date timing shifts.

series_auto.rule: yoy3: last year's same month x the summed growth of the latest 3 year-on-year pairs

methods.label: m2

p85.role: September 2025 registered births, monthly total (target prior-year same month)

p1.role: July 2026 registered births, monthly total (latest observed level)

p96.role: July 2025 registered births, monthly total (July YoY denominator)

p95.role: June 2025 registered births, monthly total (June YoY denominator)

p94.role: May 2025 registered births, monthly total (May YoY denominator)

methods.rationale: Round-1 route improved by using the kept May-June-July 2026 YoY ratios as a mean signal and the September 2025 level as the seasonal anchor. It reduces reliance on any single month but assumes the May-July decline pace persists into September; missing August 2026 and registration timing are the main failure modes.

methods.label: m3

p1.role: July 2026 registered births, monthly total (latest observed level)

p85.role: September 2025 registered births, monthly total (target prior-year same month)

p96.role: July 2025 registered births, monthly total (seasonal-ratio denominator)

methods.rationale: Round-1 route using the latest observed July 2026 level multiplied by the September-versus-July 2025 seasonal ratio. It is transparent and uses only direct birth-registration counts, but assumes the 2025 seasonal ratio transfers to 2026 and is vulnerable to month-end registration timing, including the late-September 2026 holiday in p181.

methods.label: m4

p85.role: September 2025 registered births, monthly total (target prior-year same month)

p44.role: January-February 2026 cumulative registered births (2026 early-year level)

methods.rationale: Independent early-year signal: applies the January-February 2026 versus January-February 2025 cumulative YoY ratio to the September 2025 level. It captures the sharp early-2026 decline but may overstate September weakness if the May-July 2026 moderation continues; it is not a substitute for August data.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 3 blocks, geometric mean of 2 methods sharing inputs; median of blocks: this block is the median
weight_basis.m2: B1 of 3 blocks, geometric mean of 2 methods sharing inputs; median of blocks: this block is the median
weight_basis.m3: B2 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)
weight_basis.m4: B3 of 3 blocks; median of blocks: not the median (one vote, counts in the interval)

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

m2.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

m3.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

m4.note: Monte Carlo width below the default, not used to narrow

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

baseline.rule: seasonal naive: the target's value for the same month last year

published.note: not checked: backtest or scored question (as_of before today, or an official value is registered), so the target cannot have been published by as_of

residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
